questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13981529/assets/2ab9745cb9d157e566c101a6ca79514017903fa57eaf8725c846afd272c74f93.png)

What is the equation of the ellipse given above?
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the ellipse is centered at $(3,-1),$ the horizontal radius has length $a=2,$ and the vertical radius has length $b=4.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-3)^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{(y-(-1))^{2}}{{4}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-3)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{16} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
For the ellipse $\frac{(x-6)^{2}}{49}+\frac{(y+5)^{2}}{7}=1,$ find the lengths of its major and minor axes.

$\,$ The length of the major axis is 
{{field-1}}.

$\,$ The length of the minor axis is 
{{field-2}}.
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

In the given equation, we have $h=6$ and $k=-5,$ so the center is located at $(6,-5).$

In the given equation, we also have ${a}^{2}=49$ and ${b}^{2}=7.$

- Since ${a}^{2}=49,$ the length of the horizontal radius must be $a=\sqrt{49}=7.$

- Since ${b}^{2}=7,$ the length of the vertical radius must be $b=\sqrt{7}.$

So the semi-major axis has length $a=7,$ and the semi-minor axis has length $b=\sqrt{7}.$

Therefore, the major axis has length $2a=2\cdot 7=14,$ and the minor axis has length $2b=2\cdot \sqrt{7}=2\sqrt{7}.$

$\,$ The length of the major axis is 
{{field-1}}.

$\,$ The length of the minor axis is 
{{field-2}}.
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

In the given equation, we have $h=3$ and $k=-8,$ so the center is located at $(3,-8).$

In the given equation, we also have ${a}^{2}=8$ and ${b}^{2}=81.$

- Since ${a}^{2}=8,$ the length of the horizontal radius must be $a=\sqrt{8}=2\sqrt{2}.$

- Since ${b}^{2}=81,$ the length of the vertical radius must be $b=\sqrt{81}=9.$

So the semi-major axis has length $b=9,$ and the semi-minor axis has length $a=2\sqrt{2}.$

Therefore, the major axis has length $2b=2\cdot 9=18,$ and the minor axis has length $2a=2\cdot 2\sqrt{2}=4\sqrt{2}.$
